name: warehouse
description: Data warehouse / BI pipeline (ADR-0004): a Container running dlt + dbt-duckdb extracts incrementally into a durable append-only raw layer in R2 and materializes schema-declared parquet marts from it on a daily Cron Trigger, served by a bearer-authed edge API that reads parquet directly (no container wake for reads). Ships with one reference connector (GitHub).
instructions:
The scaffolded package is generic — all per-project identity lives in the instance files, not in wrangler.jsonc.

=== 1. Secrets ===

Add these to packages/infra/environments/<env>/secrets.yaml:

  WAREHOUSE_TOKEN                  Any long random string (`openssl rand -hex 32`). Gates every route.
  WAREHOUSE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID       See "R2 credentials" below.
  WAREHOUSE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   See "R2 credentials" below.
  GITHUB_TOKEN                     Only if you keep the reference connector. A fine-grained PAT,
                                   read-only, scoped to the repo you set in GITHUB_OWNER/GITHUB_REPO.

CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN needs Workers Scripts: Edit, Workers R2 Storage: Edit, and Containers: Edit.

=== 2. R2 credentials (required — the container uploads marts directly) ===

The container runs OUTSIDE the Worker's binding graph, so it cannot use the WAREHOUSE_BUCKET
r2Binding to write. It needs real S3-compatible credentials, which R2 derives from a Cloudflare
API token — no zbc module can emit these, so they are set by hand, once:

  WAREHOUSE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID     = your Cloudflare API token's ID (shown in the dashboard token
                                   list, or via GET /user/tokens/verify -> result.id)
  WAREHOUSE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = the SHA-256 of the token's VALUE:
                                     printf '%s' "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" | shasum -a 256
  WAREHOUSE_R2_ENDPOINT          = https://<accountId>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com   (a workerVar,
                                   not a secret — it contains no credential)

=== 3. Instance files ===

Create two files in packages/infra/environments/<env>/:

   // warehouse-bucket.ts — the R2 bucket holding the marts
   import { r2Module } from '../../modules/r2'
   export default r2Module.instance({
     name: 'warehouse-bucket',
     config: { accountId: '<account id>', bucketName: '<project>-warehouse' },
   })

   // warehouse.ts — the worker + container
   import { cloudflareModule } from '../../modules/cloudflare'
   import warehouseBucket from './warehouse-bucket'
   export default cloudflareModule.instance({
     name: 'warehouse',
     imports: [warehouseBucket],
     config: {
       workdir: 'packages/warehouse',
       accountId: '<account id>',
       workerName: '<project>-warehouse',
       workerSecrets: [
         'WAREHOUSE_TOKEN',
         'GITHUB_TOKEN',
         'WAREHOUSE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID',
         'WAREHOUSE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY',
       ],
       workerVars: [
         { name: 'GITHUB_OWNER', value: '<github org/user>' },
         { name: 'GITHUB_REPO', value: '<github repo>' },
         { name: 'WAREHOUSE_BUCKET_NAME', value: '<project>-warehouse' },
         { name: 'WAREHOUSE_R2_ENDPOINT', value: 'https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com' },
       ],
       r2Bindings: [{ binding: 'WAREHOUSE_BUCKET', from: 'warehouse-bucket', output: 'bucketName' }],
       immediateContainerRollout: true,
     },
   })

All four WAREHOUSE_R2_*/WAREHOUSE_BUCKET_NAME entries are REQUIRED — the container validates them
at startup and refuses to run without them, rather than failing at the final upload.

=== 4. Apply and use ===

`zbc apply <env>` provisions the bucket and deploys the worker + container (Docker must be running
locally; the account needs a Workers Paid plan with Containers enabled). The daily Cron Trigger
(wrangler.jsonc's `triggers.crons`) runs the pipeline; trigger one immediately with
`POST /materialize` (bearer WAREHOUSE_TOKEN) instead of waiting. Read a mart with
`GET /marts/<name>` (same bearer). Both a missing and a malformed mart name return 404, by design.

=== 5. Adding a mart ===

Add a model under dbt/models/marts/ with `materialized='external'` and a `location` writing parquet
into ./marts, plus an entry in dbt/models/marts/schema.yml declaring EVERY column with a
`description` and a `data_type`. Accepted data_type values are exactly:

  VARCHAR, TIMESTAMP, BIGINT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN   (case-insensitive)

A column with no description, no data_type, or a type outside that list fails the run with an error
naming the mart and column — an undocumented mart is never published. The declared schema is also
verified against the parquet dbt actually wrote (column names AND types), so schema.yml and your
model's SELECT cannot silently drift apart.

=== 6. Adding a connector / dropping the GitHub one ===

Connectors are declared in container/connectors.ts. Add a Python module under connectors/ and add an
entry there ({ name, script, env }); its secrets go in the instance's workerSecrets and are
forwarded into the materialize run only — never readable from the mart-read API.

To drop the GitHub sample entirely: remove its entry from container/connectors.ts, delete
connectors/github.py, delete dbt/models/staging/stg_github_issues.sql and
dbt/models/marts/mart_github_issues.sql (plus its schema.yml entry), and drop GITHUB_TOKEN from
secrets.yaml and the instance. Note the pipeline requires at least one mart — it fails loudly rather
than reporting a silent success if dbt produces none.

A new connector should follow the reference one's shape: land through dlt's filesystem destination
at WAREHOUSE_RAW_URL (container/materialize.ts resolves this and injects it -- do not re-derive it),
use write_disposition 'append' with an incremental cursor, and dedupe in the staging model. Read the
raw glob with `union_by_name := true`; without it DuckDB silently drops columns that older files
lack, with no error.

=== 7. The raw layer and cursors ===

Raw lands in the SAME bucket as marts, under raw/, and is durable and append-only. That is what
makes extraction incremental: dlt persists its cursor to raw/<dataset>/_dlt_pipeline_state/ and
restores it on every cold container, so a run fetches only what changed since the last one.

Two consequences worth knowing before you debug one of them:

  * A cursor is durable when it is WRONG, too. Editing `initial_value` in a connector does NOT
    move a cursor that already exists -- the persisted value always wins. If a connector is stuck
    (runs succeed, nothing new ever lands), reset it by deleting the state prefix:

      wrangler r2 object delete <bucket>/raw/<dataset>/_dlt_pipeline_state --remote

    This is safe. Raw data is untouched; the next run re-extracts from the connector's initial
    value and the staging model dedupes the overlap away.

  * Storage grows with CHANGE VOLUME, not run count -- an unchanged source adds nothing. dlt's
    state files are capped (DESTINATION__FILESYSTEM__MAX_STATE_FILES); raw data files are not,
    and are deliberately kept: they are the history you cannot re-fetch once the source API has
    moved on. Prune with an R2 lifecycle rule if a source's churn makes that a real cost.
